tools.name: schema_overview
tools.description: Get a compact index of the entire Valets data model — every model and enum with a one-line summary. Start here, then call get_schema(name) for full detail. Pass { full: true } for the verbose summary (large; may exceed client output limits).

full.description: Return the full verbose llms.txt summary (~37k tokens) inline instead of the compact index. Default false.

tools.name: snapshot_info
tools.description: Report the provenance and freshness of the schema data this server is serving: when the snapshot was generated, how old it is, the package version, and whether it is stale. Call this to VERIFY you are reasoning against a current contract before drawing conclusions from the schema — a bundled snapshot can be arbitrarily old and is otherwise indistinguishable from a fresh one (GH#174).

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Get the JSON Schema definition for a specific model or enum. Use kebab-case names (e.g. 'order', 'payment-status', 'customer-payment').

tools.name: get_doc
tools.description: Get the raw Markdown documentation for a schema page. Use slugs like 'models/order', 'enums/payment-status', 'decisions/summary'.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search across all documentation pages for a keyword or phrase. Results are ranked so that definitions (field/property headings, schema tables) come first and example-JSON lines last; field hits are reported as `Model:field`. Returns the top matches with their best matching line.

tools.name: list_decisions
tools.description: List all data model decisions (D00-D37+) with their status and summary.

tools.name: get_decision
tools.description: Get full details for a specific data model decision by ID (e.g. 'D12', 'D22').

tools.name: get_openapi
tools.description: Get the OpenAPI 3.1 spec. Filter to a single component schema by name (PascalCase, e.g. 'Order'). With no component, returns a compact index of available component names — NOT the whole spec, which is ~88k tokens and exceeds client limits. Pass { full: true } to get the entire spec inline.

full.description: Return the entire OpenAPI spec (~88k tokens) inline. Default false → component index when no component is given.

tools.name: get_guidance
tools.description: Get use-case recipes showing which MCP tools to call and in what order. Call with no arguments for an index of all recipes, or pass a slug to get the full recipe detail.

slug.description: Recipe slug (e.g. 'write-model-code', 'field-history', 'whatsapp-conversation-display'). Omit to list all recipes.

tools.name: validate_document
tools.description: Validate a candidate document against the CANONICAL Zod schema for a model (D72). This is a real oracle, not a shape check: it runs the same Zod schema the backend runs, so cross-field .refine() rules are enforced (signed quantity, WhatsApp kind⇄payload exclusivity, price/priceDelta XOR, …) — rules the published JSON Schema physically cannot carry. Returns { valid, errors: [{ path, message, code }], strippedKeys }; code 'custom' is a cross-field rule. IMPORTANT (GH#221): the read schema STRIPS unknown keys rather than rejecting them (capture-first, D62 — a live document may carry an un-modelled field), so a document with fields the model does not declare still returns valid:true. `strippedKeys` lists any such dropped fields (dot / [i] paths); a NON-EMPTY strippedKeys means those fields are NOT in the contract and would not persist as declared — treat it as invalid for a WRITE. Only variant 'read' (the full stored document shape) is supported — 'create' and 'update' return an explicit not-supported error rather than a misleading verdict; use get_openapi('OrderCreate' / 'OrderUpdate') for the write shapes.

model.description: Model name in kebab-case, as get_schema uses (e.g. 'order', 'customer-payment', 'product-variant')

document.description: The candidate document to validate (a JSON object)

variant.description: Which shape to validate against. Default 'read'. 'create'/'update' are NOT yet supported — see the tool description.
